The daughter of Night Of Thunder went on to gain compensation for that luckless run with a Group 3 success at the Curragh the following month and has only been seen twice since. Having returned with another respectable third behind an impressive winner in the Middleton at York, James Tate's mare reverts to her optimum distance with a big chance of making her course experience count. Sirona has placed form at this level and poses a serious threat to the selection, while Bright Thunder and Skellet also have the calibre to be on the premises.

Docklands is dependable and boasts enough solid form to suggest he can be a serious player if he handles the track, while Royal Playwright is surely better than he managed in the Dante at York and could feasibly bounce back. Geography's German form stacks up well and he needs taking seriously.

selections.comment: From the likes of Shergar to Galileo and Sea The Stars, all the way to City Of Troy, who was breathtaking in this 12 months ago, it takes a real superstar to land the jewel in the crown of the Flat season. Aidan O'Brien's typically strong contingent appears to be headed by Delacroix, whose dam Tepin has already produced a stout stayer in the form of stablemate Grateful - a winner of the Prix de Royallieu at Longchamp last season. The Lion In Winter had been long touted for this contest but his no-show in the Dante behind Pride Of Arras (winner) and Damysus (second), along with stall 19, tempers enthusiasm. That pair remain of considerable interest, though 2000 Guineas winner RULING COURT is taken to rubber-stamp his credentials as the leading three-year-old. The Justify colt enters unknown territory regarding stamina, but both trainer and jockey have been extremely bullish in the build up and the pair have seldom been wrong in the past. It would be fitting were Midak, who carries the colours of the late Aga Khan, to feature, and the unbeaten Footstepsinthesand colt should not be taken lightly.

Andrew Balding's charge disappointed on soft ground in September but has not looked back since. Impressive on his return at Brighton in April before following up at Lingfield latest, a further 5lb rise in the handicap could still underestimate him. First-time cheekpieces could elicit further improvement within November Handicap fifth Valvano, who made a pleasing return at Goodwood last time. On balance his turf form mathces the levels achieved on the AW and he's gone pretty well fresh, both on his career debut and again last term. He's fallen from an introductory mark of 67 down just 53 and looks ready to gain a first career win on 15th attempt. Letter Of The Law must bounce back but was an encouraging second (albeit beaten three lengths) over course and distance on penultimate start and can challenge again off the same mark

selections.comment: Diamond Cottage and VAPE meet again having contested a similar event over CD in late May. The former got up to win late on having had to wait for a gap and has every chance of going in again. However, although Vape was only sixth that day he was beaten little over a length having endured an even tougher time close home and was never able to deliver his final kick. They were side by side in the final furlong but Diamond Cottage eventually got the clear passage. With a three pound pull Vape is taken to just get the better of the duel this time. Diamondsinthesand could run a big race back over 6f but will need to avoid being slow out the gates and losing his chance early on. If breaking close to terms he can chase the above pair home ahead of You Are Everything

selections.comment: A chance is taken with RED DEREK who returns from a break off a mark 7lb lower than when last winning back in 2022. He's been relatively lightly raced since (ten runs) and his latest run in December can be excused (very poor record on Tapeta) and the combination of easy ground a drop back to 1m4f should see him in a much better light and it's encouraging he was beaten just a length on first trun last term off a much longer layoff. He's worth chancing in a weak affair. Fiddlers Green poses the biggest threat and is arguably a more solid choice even if he needs to bounce back from a poor run last time on quick ground. He simply can't handle fast ground and much better is expected now there's give in the ground. Marioento is next on the short-list, just ahead of Innisfree Pearl

selections.comment: This is far from easy to solve with question marks about most of the runners in one way or another. Preference is just for SKELLET, who was progressive last term and may continue that upward curve this season. The worry with her is fitness since this will be her seasonal debut. Royal Dress has no such concerns, but was probably about 7lb below her best form when quite well beaten on her reappearance. The drop back from 10f to an extended mile here will probably suit her and she is entitled to come on for her first run and is a big danger. Spiritual is also to be feared. She was made plenty of use of when running to form on her first outing of the campaign. She too could come on for that run, but she only just gets a mile and will not want too much rain to have softened the ground unduly.

If he is, he has the form to win this with a bit to spare. Persica and fellow Group 3 winner Geography are the pick of the opposition ahead of last year's second, Royal Dubai.

selections.comment: Ready preference is for RULING COURT, whose 2,000 Guineas win represents very strong form (and was boosted again at Leopardstown on Thursday evening). Though he needs to prove his stamina upped in trip, connections have long thought of him as an embryonic 10f horse at least while his pedigree bears some striking similarities to last year's Derby winner City Of Troy in that both are sons of Justify whose dams were by stamina influence sires. As such - and under the unflappable William Buick - Charlie Appleby's colt can become the first 2,000 Guineas winner to take the premier Classic since Camelot in 2012. Typically for the Derby, there are a whole host of smart and highly progressive colts among the opposition with unbeaten Dante winner Pride Of Arras the most interesting of them and the main danger ahead of Damysus, second to him in that York race having again shaped as if 1m4f would suit him better. The Gosdens' colt is best of those at bigger prices and can claim minor honours. Delacroix has won his two trials this spring well but quite what he has beaten in open to question. Stablemate The Lion In Winter appeals more and he may be best of the rest. Outsiders Tennessee Stud and Nightwalker have place possibilities at big prices, with both having hinted strongly at untapped stamina reserves.

The consistent but frustrating Wee Alki looks the biggest threat and he could be tough to peg back if allowed an easy lead down in trip while Present Fair is also respected. That rival arrives in form and has won off a higher mark in the past.

selections.comment: The in form Susan Corbett holds a strong hand here with the pair at the top of the weights. Pinot Rouge returned to form under an overly aggressive ride last time and that form has been franked. She's dropped to a good mark on her novice form and is feared but it is her stablemate KILMORE ROCK who appeals most. He completed a hat trick in decisive fashion last time looking like he had more in the tank. Though an easy lead is unlikely here he is taken to continue his progress with the stable jockey on board. Powers Dilemma is another who showed improved form from the front last time. He's unexposed in handicaps on good ground and looks the biggest danger to the pair.

selections.comment: Nicky Henderson's ILE DE JERSEY was well backed when landing a mares handicap hurdle at Aintree last time out, always keeping on well and holding off the challengers. She goes back over fences now, and her record of one win in just four career starts over the larger obstacles is enough to suggest she can win once again. She runs off the same mark here as she did when she last won over fences; therefore, she could easily go in again here. Somespring Special has the most experience under her belt with ten runs over fences; she has the form figures of 122 since changing to Philip Hobbs's yard, and given her form since the change in stables, she could go well and place again here. Mermaids Cave has been running really well in hurdle races recently, and although she has only had just the one career start over fences, that could set her up nicely, as she might improve enough to run well here.

Harrys Hope is a very game mare who always runs well, and with the form figures of 212 for the new season, she could go well here but has been very busy lately.

selections.comment: Not much to go on in terms of form for these youngsters; however, the Skeltons have an excellent strike rate with their bumper horses, and their SON OF TYRAN was only beaten a neck in his sole point-to-point run 63 days ago. He was sent off joint favourite that day; therefore, the vibes were clearly strong, and he did pull a further 2 lengths plus clear of the 3rd placed horse. The Skelton's know how to get their horses fit and ready for their first runs; therefore, he is the one they will all have to beat here. Nana Noodleman pulled up on her first-ever point-to-point run, but she soon put that behind her when coming 2nd on her second run. She gets the mare's allowance here and does hail from a top yard but does have the 139-day break to overcome. Lovis De Sceaux has already had two runs in bumpers and ended up coming 2nd at Hereford just 58 days ago. He is sure to go well but might find it tricky to beat some decent prospects hailing from top-class yards.

selections.comment: ROMANY BROWN has changed hands since her victory in Killarney, and although she has a penalty to carry here, she is currently rated 122, which is a pretty high mark for some of these to reach. She has some good form in the book, plenty of experience to boot, and she is a very nice acquisition for the Ben Case team. She could easily make it back-to-back novice victories here on her UK and stable debut. Noble Miss has changed yards since winning on bumper debut at the back end of last year; she is now trained by Sarah Humphrey and looks to have a fair amount of potential judging by the manner she won on her racecourse debut last year. Squire Danagher was well beaten on hurdle debut but was very unlucky in running. With that experience under his belt and coming from a top yard, he could take a step forward here.

That pair look the biggest dangers to the selection.
